Title: ‘Let MACC, AGC look into it’: Anwar leaves Saravanan’s letter to authorities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today he would leave it to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) to examine a letter from MIC deputy president Datuk Seri M. Saravanan concerning allegations linking him to the recruitment of foreign workers.
Anwar said he would refer the contents of the letter to the relevant authorities to ensure any investigation and prosecution proceeded according to their respective jurisdictions,
Sinar Harian
reported today.
“Rather than getting to that point, it is not my business. I will refer it to MACC or the Attorney General’s Chambers for them to examine,” he told reporters outside Masjid Sembilang in Seberang Jaya today.
Anwar arrived at the mosque at about 1.15pm to perform Friday prayers and meet congregants.
He also stressed that all parties should allow the investigation and prosecution process to proceed without drawing conclusions before the matter was decided by the courts.
“We must give room for the investigation, prosecution and process to continue, and not make any statements because it is not certain until it is decided by the court,” he said.
Saravanan, who is also Tapah MP, had earlier expressed regret over what he described as baseless allegations by MACC linking him to the recruitment of foreign workers.
The former human resources minister said he had never been personally involved in the recruitment of foreign workers, nor had he involved any family members throughout his tenure.
He said a Cabinet memorandum dated April 13, 2022 also clarified that the Human Resources Minister did not have the authority to approve foreign worker recruitment, while a special one-stop centre (OSC) involving multiple ministries would be established to expedite the recruitment process.

Title: Kulai crash death reclassified as murder; 13 suspects arrested including minors
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 28 — Police have arrested 13 people, including a 15-year-old girl, to assist in investigations into the death of a 17-year-old girl in Kulai last Tuesday, which has now been reclassified as a murder case.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the Kulai district police headquarters operations room received information from the public about a road accident involving a black Perodua Myvi at the Lingkaran Bulatan Persiaran Indahpura 4 at about 12.38 am.
He said initial investigations found that the vehicle was driven by a 20-year-old man with four passengers, including the 17-year-old victim.
“All of them had just finished dinner and were travelling from Jalan Kenanga, Indahpura, to their respective homes when the victim’s car was followed by several vehicles, including a black Toyota Vellfire.
“When they reached the roundabout, the vehicle carrying the victim was believed to have been hit by the Toyota Vellfire, causing it to veer off onto the road shoulder,” he said at a press conference at the Johor Police Contingent Headquarters here today.
The impact caused the victim, a front seat passenger, to be thrown out of the vehicle after the car door was damaged.
He said the victim was believed to have been subsequently run over by the Toyota Vellfire before the vehicle sped off. The victim was pronounced dead at the scene.
Following the incident, police arrested seven men and a 15-year-old girl, aged between 15 and 31, in the first raids conducted in Johor Bahru and Selangor on Aug 25 and 26.
He said five more men, aged between 16 and 29, were arrested on Aug 27 in the Johor Bahru area.
Ab Rahaman said checks found that nine of the suspects had criminal records, while urine screening tests on all 13 suspects returned negative for drugs.
Police also seized 12 mobile phones, a Kia Forte, a Toyota Vellfire, a Toyota Hilux pickup truck, as well as two metal rods comprising a baton and a baseball bat.
He said the Magistrate’s Court had granted seven days’ remand from Aug 26 to Sept 1 for seven suspects, while one suspect was remanded for two days on Aug 27 and 28.
The five suspects arrested in follow-up operations were taken to the Kulai Magistrate’s Court today for remand applications.
The investigation is being conducted under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder and Section 148 of the Penal Code for possessing weapons during a riot, while the Johor Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department is conducting a parallel investigation under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He said the incident was believed to be linked to a membership conflict between two secret society groups in the Johor Bahru area, although the actual motive is still under investigation. — Bernama

Title: Friends face murder charge over killing of Indonesian man in Klang’s Telok Gong
Article:
KLANG, Aug 28 — Two friends were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of an Indonesian man earlier this month.
Muhd Asnawi Ghazali, 37, and Musa Ramli, 25, nodded in understanding after the charges were read out before Magistrate Siti Zubaidah Mahat.
However, no plea was recorded from either accused, as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
According to the charge, the pair, together with another man still at large known as Kutek, are accused of killing Suherman, 47, at an unnumbered house in Kampung Baru Telok Gong, here, around 6.30 am on Aug 6.
They were charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years. If not sentenced to death, they shall also be liable to not less than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Mohammad Uzzair Rosman appeared for the prosecution, while both accused were unrepresented.
The court set Nov 27 for the next mention of the case. — Bernama

Title: Thousands watch National Day rehearsal at Dataran Putrajaya ahead of Aug 31 parade
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — The excitement surrounding the 2026 National Day celebrations is building as crowds flock to the iconic Dataran Putrajaya to witness first-hand the preparations and parade rehearsals ahead of the historic celebration on Aug 31.
As early as 6.30 am, visitors began filling the seats provided and the surrounding areas to witness the lively pre-rehearsal parade, including the impressive display by security forces and the Rebana Ubi musical performance that added to the National Day’s lively atmosphere.
Participants and visitors met by Bernama described the nearly two-hour parade rehearsal as an important platform for instilling patriotism and fostering love for the country, particularly among the younger generation.
For Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) personnel Mohd Helmi Masuhudi, 38, who took part in the Jalur Gemilang flag-raising ceremony, the task was a great honour for him and his team.
“Representing the RMN at this grand occasion is a source of great pride. Every time we take part in the National Day celebrations, it reminds us of the harmony, peace and unity among Malaysia’s various races that we enjoy today,” he said after completing the rehearsal.
For Nur Alya Natasya Muhamad Solehin, 24, her presence was not merely to add to the National Day celebrations, but also to show moral support for her father, who was directly involved in the parade.
“This is my first time coming to watch the rehearsal. Although I brought along my four-month-old baby, I am still excited because my father is taking part in the Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) contingent this year,” she said.
Members of the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM) contingent march during the rehearsal for the National Day 2026 celebration at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 28, 2026. — Bernama pic
Also sharing her excitement at witnessing the lively parade and procession was retired Siti Haidah Idris, 68, from Rembau, Negeri Sembilan, who said watching the rehearsal live offered a different experience compared with watching it on television.
“This is the first time in my life that I have watched a rehearsal in person. Although I arrived a little late, I am very happy to be able to bring my grandchild to see the displays of unity as well as the parade of military and police assets,” she said.
Customs officer Nurshazarina Abd Karim, 43, took the opportunity to spend her leave with her husband and four children to experience the festive atmosphere first-hand, while also wanting to instil in her children a spirit of patriotism through the display of assets and aerial performances.
Meanwhile, goods supplier Hafizur Rahman Azzaharuddin, 27, who travelled from Kota Damansara with his wife and young child, expressed his admiration for the performances, describing them as spirited, energetic and full of colour.
“I really wanted to see the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) and Malaysian Army (TDM) contingents. It was definitely worth coming, even if it was just to watch the rehearsal,” he said.
For participant R. Tarishini, 26, who represented a dance troupe, taking part in the parade for the first time was an unforgettable experience, as she had the opportunity to showcase the beauty of the country’s cultural arts before thousands of spectators while fostering a spirit of unity and patriotism.
The rehearsal held today saw various parade contingents, cultural performances and security asset displays undergoing final preparations to ensure the smooth running of the National Day celebrations on Aug 31.
Themed ‘Malaysia MADANI: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati’, the 69th National Day celebration will be held at Dataran Putrajaya, with more than 80,000 visitors expected to attend. — Bernama

Title: Haze continues choking Malaysia as 19 areas see ‘Unhealthy’ air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Nineteen air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded “unhealthy” air pollutant index (API) readings as of 1.30pm today, according to Department of Environment (DoE) data.
The highest API reading nationwide was logged at Serian in Sarawak, which reached 181. Cheras in the federal capital followed with 160, while two stations in Penang, namely Minden (159) and Seberang Perai (158), alongside Sarikei in Sarawak (158), rounded out the most severely affected areas.
An API reading between 101 and 200 is categorised as “unhealthy,” while 201 to 300 is “very unhealthy” and anything above 300 is deemed “hazardous.”
The Greater Klang Valley, including Putrajaya, accounted for six of the 19 stations in the unhealthy bracket.
Cheras recorded the region’s poorest air quality at 160, the second-highest reading nationally, while Batu Muda, Shah Alam, and Johan Setia were all tied at 152. Putrajaya stood at 145, while Petaling Jaya registered 129.
The persistent layer of smog over the Klang Valley prompted the government to relocate the National Day 2026 Prime Minister’s Address on August 30 from Dataran Merdeka to the indoor Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC).
Event organisers cited the need to protect the “safety, health and comfort” of guests and members of the public amid worsening atmospheric conditions.
Unhealthy levels across other states
Beyond Sarawak and the Klang Valley, deteriorating air quality was observed across several northern and central states.
In the north, Perak registered elevated readings in Taiping (155) and Tasek Ipoh (150), while Penang’s Seberang Jaya stood at 154. In Kedah, Sungai Petani and Alor Setar logged readings of 153 and 145 respectively.
Further south in Peninsular Malaysia, Seremban in Negeri Sembilan posted an API reading of 115.
The haze has lingered across Peninsular Malaysia and western Borneo over the past week.
Authorities have stepped up bilateral preventive coordination with Indonesia to mitigate transboundary smoke, warning that dry weather conditions linked to El Niño could exacerbate fire risks heading into October.
The Ministry of Health has advised the public, particularly vulnerable groups, to limit outdoor activities and monitor official air quality updates through the DoE’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).

Title: Heavy rain and strong winds expected across Johor, Sabah and Sarawak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning covering multiple states, effective until 4:00 pm today.
In Johor, the warning covers Pontian, Kulai, Johor Bahru and Kota Tinggi.
In Sarawak, affected areas include Bintulu and Sebauh in the Bintulu district; Miri, Subis, Beluru and Marudi in the Miri district; and Mukah, Dalat and Matu in the Mukah district.
In Sabah, the warning applies to Kuala Penyu, Beaufort, Membakut, Keningau, Tambunan and Tenom in the Interior division, as well as Papar, Penampang, Putatan, Kota Kinabalu, Tuaran and Kota Belud along the West Coast. Labuan is also included.
Residents in these areas should brace for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds.
According to MetMalaysia, such warnings are issued when rainfall intensity is expected to exceed 20 mm/hour, or when storms are likely to persist for more than an hour.
Thunderstorm warnings remain valid for a maximum of six hours from issuance.
The public is advised to stay updated on further alerts and take necessary precautions against flash floods, strong winds and lightning.

Title: Anwar begins two-day Penang visit with students, community events and Scout jamboree
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today began a two-day working visit to Penang packed with various engagements, including meetings with students, the Muslim community and local residents.
The visit began with Friday prayers at Masjid Sembilang, Butterworth, at 1.30pm, followed by a “Temu Anwar Bersama Pelajar” session in conjunction with the Ambang Merdeka Sahabat Madani Programme at the Tuanku Bainun Teacher Education Institute campus in Bukit Mertajam at 4pm.
The event, which will also be attended by Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, provides students with an opportunity to interact directly with the country’s top leader.
The prime minister will wrap up the first day’s agenda by attending a Maulid Akbar event in conjunction with Independence Day at Masjid Jamek Tengah Berapit, Bukit Mertajam, at 9 pm.
Tomorrow, Anwar is scheduled to officiate the Permatang Pauh Skim Usahawan Bangkit programme at Dewan Yayasan Aman Penanti, Kubang Semang, at 10am.
He will then attend the National-Level Tadabbur Perdana Programme and the Permatang Pauh Maidah Wanita Madani Programme at Masjid Muhajirin, Seberang Jaya, at 11.30am.
In the afternoon, the finance minister will officiate the 15th Malaysian Scout Jamboree at the Penang State Stadium in Batu Kawan, which will bring together more than 5,450 local and international scouts from 11 countries, including South Korea, Indonesia, Singapore and Sri Lanka.
This year’s jamboree marks a historic occasion as the national event returns to Penang after 60 years, since the state first hosted it in Teluk Bahang in 1966.
Anwar is then scheduled to attend the 2026 Ambang Merdeka Sahabat Madani Programme finale at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Permatang Pauh at 4pm, bringing his visit to Penang to a close. — Bernama

Title: Wisma Putra launches round-the-clock effort to trace 57 Malaysians after Nepal disaster
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Fifty-seven Malaysians are currently uncontactable following devastating floods in Nepal’s Rasuwa district, with Wisma Putra’s Operations Room now operating around the clock as diplomatic missions cross-check reports with Nepalese authorities.
Wisma Putra, Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry, said in a statement on Friday that the latest figure was based on reports received from family members, friends and employers as of 11 pm on Aug 27.
Malaysian diplomatic missions in the region are cross-checking the reports against information obtained from relevant Nepalese authorities and agencies, while also working with the Emergency Response Team of Nepal’s Foreign Ministry and the Nepal Tourism Board to verify information on those who remain uncontactable, it said.
The ministry said local authorities had reported the rescue of 31 foreign nationals thus far.
“At this stage, the ministry has not received confirmation that any Malaysians are among those rescued,” it said.
Wisma Putra said it had also received information that Malaysian nationals may have entered the affected areas through neighbouring China and India.
“In view of this, family members of Malaysians travelling in the wider region who have yet to register their presence are urged to provide their details to the ministry,” it said.
The ministry’s Operations Room in Putrajaya is now operating on a 24-hour basis until further notice to coordinate information and provide direct support to Malaysians in the affected areas and their families.
Family members with relevant information, including full names, passport numbers, travel itineraries, last known locations and contactable telephone numbers, are urged to contact the ministry at +603 8887 4570 (telephone) or dutyofficer@kln.gov.my (email).
They may also provide the relevant details directly to the Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu via email at mwkathmandu@kln.gov.my, with a copy sent to the ministry’s Operations Room.
Malaysians are also urged to register and regularly update their contact details via the e-Konsular portal at
https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my
.
“Malaysians residing in or travelling through Nepal, particularly those in or near the affected areas, are strongly advised to remain vigilant, prioritise their personal safety and adhere to all instructions issued by the local authorities,” said Wisma Putra.
The floods, which struck on Wednesday morning, have claimed more than 400 lives, with more than 800 others, including hundreds of foreign tourists, still unaccounted for as search and rescue operations continue amid widespread damage to roads and communication disruptions.
In Nepal, police, security agencies, local authorities and residents continue search and rescue operations across the flood-affected areas, while families are also being evacuated from locations at risk of further flooding.
With road access severely disrupted and communications cut off across much of the affected region, helicopters are being used extensively in ongoing operations.
Individuals requiring immediate medical attention are being airlifted to major hospitals in Kathmandu, while those with minor injuries are being treated at medical camps in the affected areas. — Bernama

Title: Saravanan calls graft charges ‘wild accusations’, says facts will emerge in court
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan today described the corruption charges against him as “wild accusations”, saying he was surprised by the three charges and had no personal relationship with the people named in them.
Speaking to reporters after claiming trial to all three charges at the Sessions Court here, the Tapah MP said he would let the facts be brought before the court.
Saravanan also appeared to suggest that the charges could be politically motivated.
“I was surprised with the charges. I won't say they are baseless; I will say they are wild accusations. The facts will be brought in court.
“The important thing is, I have no relation with the people mentioned in court earlier. I don't know them. Except for Syed Amirul, the rest I don't know, and even then, I don't have a personal relationship with Syed Amirul. These will be discussed further in court.
“Secondly, if this is your method of trying to bring me down, then send your best candidate to contest me in Tapah. Don't use these sorts of tactics to bring down a politician.
“I don't feel ashamed at all, as when the facts come out, you will be embarrassed. The people will see how you tried to accuse me with false evidence,” he added, without specifically naming anyone.
Earlier today, Saravanan, 58, pleaded not guilty to three charges of corruptly receiving a total of RM1.097 million in bribes linked to the approval of 1,000 foreign-worker quotas for TYKB Engineering Sdn Bhd.
The first charge alleges that he received RM150,000 in cash from Vectica Resources Sdn Bhd director Tan Teck Lim through Syed Amirul Syed Ahmad on June 16, 2022, at Bukit Jalil Golf & Country Resorts.
The second charge alleges that he received another RM350,000 in cash from Tan through Syed Amirul on July 7, 2022, at Jalan Telawi 3, Bangsar.
The third charge alleges that Saravanan received RM597,000 from Tan through Syed Amirul on the same day via a Maybank Islamic cheque deposited into an account belonging to Big Seven Ventures Sdn Bhd.
All three charges were framed under Section 16(a)(B) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 and are punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act.
If convicted, he faces up to 20 years in jail and a fine of at least five times the amount or value of the gratification involved, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
Saravanan, who is also MIC deputy president, served as human resources minister from 2020 to 2022.

Title: Malaysia aims to push medical device exports beyond RM50b by 2030, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Malaysia should aim to surpass RM50 billion in medical device exports by 2030, up from RM34.54 billion recorded last year.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the export target was one of three ambitions proposed to measure the country’s progress in developing its medical technology (MedTech) industry by 2030.
“We have the manufacturing base, market access and global confidence.
“But the next phase of export growth must increasingly come from higher-value products,” he said at the closing ceremony of the International Medical Device Exhibition and Conference (IMDEC) 2026 here today.
The second ambition is to develop at least 10 Malaysian MedTech champions capable of competing regionally and globally.
Ahmad Zahid said Malaysia would continue welcoming leading international MedTech companies while developing local firms that create the technology, own intellectual property and compete internationally.
The third ambition is for at least 50 per cent of jobs created by new MedTech investments by 2030 to be managerial, technical and supervisory (MTS) positions.
He said the medical device sector’s MTS index stood at only 33.1 per cent in 2025.
“Capital may enter Malaysia, but capability must remain in Malaysia. If we are serious about calling this a high-value industry, then the jobs it creates must increasingly be high-value jobs as well,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Technical and Vocational Education and Training Council chairman, said talent must be developed before investments arrive, rather than only after companies face workforce shortages.
“Do not come to us only when you need workers. Come earlier. Help shape programmes, identify future skills, provide industrial exposure and open more apprenticeship pathways,” he said.
In 2025, RM4 billion in new medical device investments was approved across 46 projects, creating nearly 3,400 employment opportunities.
The global medical device industry, valued at more than US$572 billion (RM2.3 trillion) last year, is projected to exceed US$1 trillion by 2034.
Held from August 26 to 28, IMDEC 2026 brought together more than 160 exhibitors and over 50 regional and international speakers in regulation, innovation and healthcare transformation. — Bernama

Title: ‘My only hope is they are safe’: A Malaysian family’s agonising wait for news after Nepal-Tibet floods
Article:
BIDUR (Nepal), Aug 28 — They came to the Himalayas seeking spiritual renewal, drawn by Tibet’s sacred, snow-capped Mount Kailash.
Instead, many pilgrims were caught in deadly floods that tore through the Nepal-Tibet region, wiping out entire villages.
“I saw two buses carrying Indian pilgrims to Kailash Mansarovar,” said 27-year-old Laloma, a Nepali mother.
She was rescued yesterday from Nepal’s devastated area of Syabrubesi, along with her infant son and husband, after sheltering for a freezing night in a school. The buses were swept away, she said.
“They are all gone,” she told AFP.
Mount Kailash is sacred to Hindus, Buddhists and Jains.
Hindus regard Kailash as the abode of deities Shiva and Parvati, while Tibetan Buddhists associate it with Mount Meru, which they say is the centre of the universe.
It is forbidden to climb the 6,638m-high mountain.
Instead, pilgrims undertake a roughly 52km contemplative circuit around its base, taking most walkers about three days.
For those en route or returning from the isolated, pyramid-shaped peak and bathing in the frigid ice waters of nearby Lake Mansarovar, across China’s frontier with Nepal, it was meant to be a healing journey of peace.
But climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of glacial lake floods and glacial collapses.
On Wednesday morning, a tsunami-like wall of water and mud powered down, caused by a glacial collapse that sent a torrent of debris downstream, burying homes and sweeping away bridges.
More than 470 people are dead and upwards of 1,400 others are missing in both China and Nepal.
‘Share your pain’
Indian spiritual leader Sadhguru this year led devotees to Kailash, an annual pilgrimage growing in popularity, especially among Indians.
Thousands of Indians are reported to have undertaken the pilgrimage this year, as well as Hindus from other nations.
Sadhguru’s “sacred walks”, organised by his Isha Foundation, promised a journey to a place “of divine connection, where the veil between the physical and spiritual is thin”.
Yesterday, he wept as he described his frantic calls to missing devotees, in a video message posted from Tibet to his several million followers.
Some 77 pilgrims were at the Nepal-China border office when floodwaters swept through the centre on Wednesday, he said in a post, alongside a terrifying video from the Chinese side of the frontier, when a wall of mud and debris crashed over the building.
“Literally, the entire group was there in the building, this is a terrible and extraordinary event,” he said, as anguished wails from other pilgrims with him are heard over the video.
“All of us, including the volunteers and support teams are deeply anguished,” the Hindu guru, whose real name is Jagdish Vasudev, added.
“To the families and loved ones of those in our group and hundreds of others who are affected in the region, I share your pain,” he added.
“All phones are off, telecommunications are down, roads are blocked, we are unable to go there,” he said, tears in his eyes.
For Indians, the pilgrimage to Kailash and Lake Mansarovar is organised annually by New Delhi’s foreign ministry, in coordination with Chinese authorities.
It restarted in 2025 for Indians for the first time since a 2020 border clash.
‘Pure intention’
Logadarrsiny Raman, 26, from Malaysia, said four members of her family were among 17 Malaysians travelling with a Nepali travel operator.
Her parents, aunt and uncle had spent months planning the pilgrimage, which they regarded as a spiritual journey and fulfilment.
“They felt like this was the right time for them to go for this pilgrimage,” Raman said, speaking to AFP in Kuala Lumpur.
“It was a very pure intention, and that’s why they wanted to go together as a family.”
She last exchanged WhatsApp messages with her father just after dawn in Nepal on Wednesday.
After that, the family heard nothing.
Raman said the travel agency told her its last contact with the group was at 8:18 am Nepal time, when they were travelling towards the Nepal-China border.
The flood crashed into the area where they last were soon after.
“I’m very anxious,” she said. “My only hope is to hear back from them that they are safe.”
She appealed for help locating her parents and the other Malaysian pilgrims.
“There’s nothing else that we all want as a family,” she said. — AFP

Title: Husband and wife among seven held as Penang police seize drugs worth RM3.2m
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 28 — A husband and wife were among seven people arrested in several operations by the Penang Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (JSJN) this month, with drugs worth more than RM3.2 million seized.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said the couple were among four people arrested in an operation in Tanjung Tokong between August 15 and 16,
Sinar Harian
reported.
He said the four comprised three local men and a local woman aged between 23 and 35.
“During the operation, police seized 38.3kg of cannabis powder, 11.47kg of cannabis flower, 4,004 Erimin 5 pills, 14kg of methamphetamine, 5kg of ketamine and 16kg of ecstasy pills.
“All the drugs seized were estimated to be worth more than RM1.17 million and the case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952,” he said at a press conference at the Penang Contingent Police Headquarters here today.
Dennis said all four suspects were remanded for 13 days from August 16 to 28 to assist investigations.
In a separate operation, a team from the Seberang Perai Utara District Police Headquarters’ Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division arrested a 23-year-old local man in Butterworth at about 6pm on August 15.
He said a search led to the seizure of about 3kg of methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) powder worth more than RM450,000.
“The suspect was remanded for five days from August 16 to 20 before being released on bail on the instructions of the deputy public prosecutor pending the chemical analysis report,” he said.
Following this, police arrested a 46-year-old local man at about 10pm in Butterworth on August 19.
“Police seized about 1.3kg of MDMA powder worth more than RM10,000 from the suspect.
“The suspect was remanded for six days from August 20 to 25,” he said.
Meanwhile, at about 10.50pm on August 22, police from the Seberang Perai Tengah District Police Headquarters’ Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division arrested a 28-year-old local man in Bukit Mertajam.
Dennis said police seized 8.4kg of MDMA powder, 1,755 ecstasy pills, 1,000 Erimin 5 pills, 0.63kg of ketamine and nine cartridges of liquid methamphetamine, with a total estimated value of more than RM1.38 million.
“The suspect was remanded for seven days from August 23 to 29 for investigation under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
“Intelligence showed that all the suspects are believed to have been actively involved in drug trafficking around Penang since May. Urine screening found four suspects positive for morphine, amphetamine and methamphetamine.
“Checks of past records found that five suspects had previous criminal and narcotics records,” he said.
He added that police also seized items estimated to be worth RM89,000 under the Dangerous Drugs (Forfeiture of Property) Act 1988.
“This success was the result of continuous intelligence gathering by JSJN and cooperation from the public. The Royal Malaysia Police will not compromise with anyone involved in drug trafficking.
“Members of the public with information on drug trafficking activities can channel it through the JSJN hotline at 012-208 7222,” he said.

Title: National Day parade preparations in Putrajaya nearly complete ahead of tomorrow’s full rehearsal, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — Preparations for the 2026 National Day parade at Dataran Putrajaya are expected to be nearly 100 per cent complete by tomorrow’s dress rehearsal, with only a few minor aspects requiring fine-tuning, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the improvements involved coordinating the movement distances between contingents to ensure the overall parade was conducted in a neater and more orderly manner.
“There are several contingents whose movements are somewhat far from the preceding contingent, so (this aspect) needs to be tightened up a little. Insya-Allah, by tomorrow (the full rehearsal), we believe (preparations) will be nearly 100 per cent complete,” he said.
Fahmi, who is also chairman of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) Main Committee, told reporters this after inspecting the rehearsal for the celebrations here today, which was also attended by Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah.
He said favourable weather conditions had helped ensure the smooth running of the rehearsal, while praising the high spirits and strong morale displayed by all participants, including security personnel and school students from three states involved in the human graphics performance.
He said that apart from new assets and formations, the inaugural participation of the Johor Military Force as well as the maritime asset, the Ibrahim-class boat designed by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, were among the main attractions of this year’s celebrations.
Fahmi gave an assurance that the safety of the multi-level structure accommodating 1,500 students for the human graphics performance had been thoroughly assessed by Putrajaya Corporation (PPj).
He said the slight movement visible on the structure was within the permitted tolerance level to accommodate the participants’ rhythmic movements.
“The structure needs to have a slight degree of movement tolerance and its safety has been ensured. This is also the third time it has been used, and so far, there have been no problems,” he said.
Regarding the structure’s slightly asymmetrical positioning, he explained that this was because the parade route and the PPj building were not on the same axis, in addition to the number of participants being reduced from 2,000 to 1,500 this year.
However, Fahmi said he had asked the organising secretariat to review the technical adjustments for future editions to reduce negative perceptions regarding the positioning of the structure. — Bernama

Title: WCE expects more traffic as Malaysians hit the road for National Day, school holidays
Article:
IPOH, Aug 28 — The West Coast Expressway (WCE) expects traffic on its operational stretches to exceed 150,000 vehicles a day during the 69th National Day celebrations and school holidays.
WCE said the increase is expected due to more people travelling to their hometowns and between states, particularly between the Klang Valley and destinations in Selangor and Perak.
Its Highway Operations head Syed Muhd Naguib Syed Mohd advised motorists to plan their journeys early and avoid peak hours, particularly from late afternoon to night.
“Our priority is the safety of every highway user. Plan your journey, get enough rest and never compromise safety just to save a few minutes,” he said in a statement today.
He said WCE would step up operational readiness along its open stretches, including 24-hour highway patrols, Emergency Response Teams (ERT) and continuous traffic monitoring.
Motorists are encouraged to use the WCE App for navigation and real-time traffic updates, including live CCTV footage, while emergency assistance is available through the WCE Infoline at 1700-81-6600, which operates 24 hours.
WCE also reminded motorists, particularly during the expected traffic surge, to ensure their vehicles are roadworthy, obey speed limits and use the emergency lane only when necessary. Motorcycle shelters are available along the highway for riders to rest or seek shelter from rain. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian Fire Dept ready to deploy specialist rescue team to Nepal as nine hikers remain uncontactable
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — The Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) is ready to deploy its Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Malaysia (STORM) team to Nepal at any time, even at short notice, should it receive instructions from the government.
JBPM director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the deployment of the team, however, would be subject to a request from the Nepalese government as well as instructions and coordination by the Foreign Ministry and the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma).
“We have prepared the best team, particularly from STORM, with the required skills and initial documentation to enable them to be deployed as quickly as possible. If instructions are received, even at short notice, we are ready to move,” he told reporters when met at the 2026 National Day parade rehearsal here today.
He said the preparations were made based on JBPM’s experience in participating in a search and rescue mission in Turkiye previously, which required personnel and travel documents to be prepared in advance.
In a related development, Nor Hisham said JBPM had still been unable to contact the nine hikers, including two department officers, as well as a local agent in Nepal as of this morning.
“We remain hopeful that communication lines there can be restored and that, at the very least, we can obtain some indication of their location and condition,” he said.
He explained that the trip was a private one and was not organised or managed by JBPM.
The members who took part in the trip were experienced hikers, and some were part of the core team that assisted in preparations for a JBPM climber’s attempt to scale Mount Everest last year.
However, he said the trip this time was more of a trekking expedition, with most of the route covered by four-wheel-drive vehicles and only the final one to two hours requiring travel on foot.
The group departed on August 24 and was expected to enter the Tibet border area on August 26.
The last communication was received while the group was having breakfast that morning, but it could not be ascertained whether they were still at their accommodation or had already set off.
“Based on the last photo and location, they were believed to have been in the area. If they started moving at around 8.30 am, we hope they managed to make their way to the higher trekking route. However, this has yet to be confirmed,” he said.
Nor Hisham said JBPM was also in close contact with the families of the officers involved, who were now using various channels and contacts in Nepal to obtain the latest information.
“We pray for the best and hope all the participants are safe,” he said.
Floods and landslides occurred along the Nepal border, affecting the Gyirong Port border crossing in Gyirong County, China, on Wednesday morning.
The death toll from the floods and landslides in Nepal has risen to 389, while 466 people were injured. — Bernama

Title: Driver trapped, suffers broken arm in four-vehicle crash on Subang route towards Federal Highway
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — A driver was trapped and suffered a broken arm in a four-vehicle crash along the Subang route towards the Federal Highway this morning.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the department received an emergency call at 9.24am before five personnel from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene, according to
Berita Harian
today.
“The fire engine arrived at 9.45am and found that the crash involved a tour bus and three cars.
“The tour bus was not carrying any passengers at the time, while a 36-year-old man was found trapped in the driver’s seat of a Honda City,” he said in a statement today.
Ashrul Riezal said firefighters managed to extricate the victim, who had suffered a broken arm, before handing him over to Health Ministry personnel for further treatment.

Title: New Batam-Penang flights to boost tourism, medical travel, says state exco
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 28 — Batik Air will launch direct flights between Batam and Penang from October 18, opening a new gateway for Penang to tap into the tourism market in Indonesia’s Riau Islands.
State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the route, the first scheduled direct air link between Batam and Penang, would operate three times a week.
“This route opens up opportunities for Penang to tap into new regional tourism markets in the Riau Islands and is an important step in expanding Indonesia as a source market while exploring new visitor segments with strong potential,” he said in a statement today.
He said Batam, located about 30 kilometres south of Singapore, was one of the key economic, industrial, commercial and tourism centres in the Riau Islands, with a strategic position in the regional connectivity between Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore.
Wong said Indonesia was already one of Penang’s key international tourism markets, with visitors from the country consistently ranking among the top international tourist arrivals to the state.
He said 201,657 Indonesian tourists entered Penang through Penang International Airport (PIA) from January to July this year, compared with 192,823 in the same period last year, an increase of 4.58 per cent.
Wong said the main Indonesian cities traditionally serving as key tourism markets for Penang included Medan, Jakarta, Surabaya and Banda Aceh, while the new route would extend the state’s reach to the Riau Islands.
He said the Batam-Penang route also had strong potential to support the state’s medical tourism sector, given Penang’s comprehensive medical facilities, professional healthcare services and well-established medical tourism ecosystem.
“With direct air connectivity between Batam and Penang, we have an opportunity to further tap into the medical tourism market in the Riau Islands and turn passenger flows into broader economic benefits and tourism spending,” he said.
Wong said the new route would also add an important component to Penang’s South-east Asian air network, particularly at a time when short-haul Asean markets were playing an important role in supporting the stability of the tourism industry.
Flight OD359 from Hang Nadim International Airport in Batam will depart at 11.30am local time and arrive at PIA at 1.55pm.
For the Penang-Batam sector, flight OD358 is scheduled to depart at 10.10am and arrive at Hang Nadim International Airport at 10.50am local time, with ticket bookings for the route now open via Batik Air’s official website. — Bernama

Title: Kedah teacher transferred pending probe into Year Four pupil’s death after sports activity
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Aug 28 — A teacher believed to be involved in the case of an 11-year-old girl who allegedly died from a heart condition after being forced to participate in sports activities has been transferred pending the outcome of an investigation, according to the Kedah Education Department (JPN).
A Kedah JPN spokesman said the teacher was transferred to another school shortly after an initial investigation, describing the move as an early intervention.
“The matter has been referred to the Integrity Unit of the Education Ministry (MOE) for further action.
“The public is urged not to speculate about the case and to give JPN and the MOE room to conduct a thorough investigation,” the spokesman told Bernama today.
Meanwhile, an internal school source said the incident involving the pupil happened on April 14, when she was reportedly involved in a selection trial for the 80-metre race for the school’s sports event.
“The pupil had a history of heart disease since childhood. (After taking part in the sports activity), she fell ill and began receiving treatment on April 17. She did not attend school for four months, and a complaint was lodged by her family on May 10,” the source said.
Earlier, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek instructed the MOE Integrity Unit to take further action over the death of Nur Qaira Alisha Ahmad ‘Ilwan, a pupil at a primary school in Kedah, in accordance with the prevailing rules and laws.
She was also informed that Kedah JPN had investigated the complaint lodged by the girl’s family.
Previously, the victim’s father’s social media post went viral, alleging that his daughter, who had a heart condition, was instructed by a teacher to participate in a running activity during the selection for the school’s sports teams although a medical letter confirming her condition had been submitted.
Following the incident, Nur Qaira Alisha was allegedly bedridden and had to be placed on oxygen before she was reported to have died at 7.49pm last Wednesday. — Bernama

Title: Saravanan claims trial to three corruption charges involving RM1.097m, granted RM450,000 bail
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan today claimed trial to three charges of corruptly receiving RM1.097 million in bribes linked to the approval of 1,000 foreign-worker quotas for a company.
The 58-year-old Tapah MP pleaded not guilty after the charges were read before Sessions Court judge Azura Alwi.
The three charges involve alleged bribes of RM150,000, RM350,000 and RM597,000, which the prosecution claims Saravanan received from Vectica Resources Sdn Bhd director Tan Teck Lim through Syed Amirul Syed Ahmad.
According to the first charge, Saravanan allegedly received RM150,000 in cash from Tan through Syed Amirul on June 16, 2022, at Bukit Jalil Golf & Country Resorts.
The payment was allegedly an inducement for Saravanan, then the human resources minister, to approve an application for 1,000 foreign-worker quotas for TYKB Engineering Sdn Bhd.
For the second charge, Saravanan allegedly received RM350,000 in cash from Tan through Syed Amirul on July 7, 2022, at Jalan Telawi 3, Bangsar.
The prosecution alleges the money was given as a reward for Saravanan approving the same application for 1,000 foreign-worker quotas for TYKB Engineering.
The third charge alleges that Saravanan received RM597,000 from Tan through Syed Amirul on the same day.
The money was allegedly paid through a Maybank Islamic cheque numbered 273704, which was deposited into a Maybank Islamic account belonging to Big Seven Ventures Sdn Bhd at the bank’s Jalan Klang Lama branch.
The prosecution again alleges the payment was a reward for Saravanan approving TYKB Engineering’s application for 1,000 foreign-worker quotas.
All three charges were framed under Section 16(a)(B) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 and are punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act.
Upon conviction, the offence carries a maximum 20-year jail term and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the bribe, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
When arguing for bail, the deputy public prosecutors, led by Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib, said the offences were non-bailable.
However they suggested bail at RM800,000 with one local surer.
Saravanan would also be required to surrender his passport, report to the closest MACC office once every three months and not be allowed to talk to the witnesses.
Saravanan’s lawyer, Geethan Ram Vincent, argued that his client had been cooperative throughout the process and was an MP who regularly attended Parliament.
He also said his client posed no flight risk and would not interfere with witnesses, and asked for bail to be set at RM300,000.
Judge Azura Alwi subsequently set bail at RM450,000 and ordered him to report to the nearest MACC office once every three months and refrain from contacting witnesses directly or indirectly.
The court set the next date for September 29.
Saravanan, who is also MIC deputy president, served as human resources minister from 2020 to 2022.
He has previously denied wrongdoing in relation to the allegations and said he would defend himself in court.

Title: Sarawak moves to tackle connectivity gaps in Limbang, Lawas
Article:
LAWAS, Aug 28 — Sarawak’s telecommunications modernisation agenda is prioritising efforts to address connectivity disruptions in northern Sarawak, particularly in Limbang and Lawas.
Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan said the collaboration between the Ministry of Utilities and Telecommunications, Sarawak Digital Economy Corporation (SEDC) and Sarawak Energy Berhad (SEB) would help improve digital connectivity and government services.
“We welcome the collaboration between SEB and SEDC to improve digital connectivity, particularly in northern Sarawak involving Limbang and Lawas.
“This is a necessity, especially as Sarawak is focusing on the digital economy. I hope that through the collaboration between SEDC and SEB, internet connectivity can be improved. This is important for us, including in further enhancing government services,” he said.
Awang Tengah, who is Bukit Sari assemblyman, said this after witnessing the exchange of Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) for the Digitisation of Connectivity in Limbang and Lawas, here yesterday.
He said the issue needed to be addressed immediately to bridge the digital divide between urban and rural areas.
“Besides that, telecommunications services also need to be improved at enforcement, security and rescue agencies,” he said.
He said better connectivity would enable these agencies to respond more swiftly to problems reported by the public.
“Education, healthcare, business and security now require fast connectivity,” he added.
Awang Tengah said businesses in Lawas were facing problems with e-payment services, while the Lawas district police headquarters was also experiencing internet connectivity issues despite its important role in disaster management and other matters.
“If we can improve this and make communication easier, action can be taken more quickly,” he said.
Also present were State Minister of Utility and Telecommunication Dato Sri Julaihi Narawi, Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah, and SEDC chairman and SEB board member Tan Sri Datuk Amar Mohamad Morshidi Abdul Ghani. — The Borneo Post

Title: Higher Education Ministry begins steps towards repeal of UUCA, halts student disciplinary proceedings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — The Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) is taking immediate steps to expand students’ freedom of expression and right to association, following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s call for the repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU).
In a statement today, the ministry said Anwar had stressed during the 13th Malaysia Madani Scholars Forum that measures to give students greater freedom should be implemented immediately while a new legal framework is being developed, without waiting for the entire process of drafting a new law to be completed.
MOHE said it had reviewed measures that could be implemented under the existing legal framework to give effect to the prime minister’s directive.
It identified several provisions under AUKU and the Student Disciplinary Rules that restrict students’ freedom of expression and association for exemption from enforcement as immediate measures.
These include freedom in the management of student associations and clubs, management of student activities, as well as freedom of expression, assembly, use of communication platforms and the distribution and publication of documents.
“Accordingly, MOHE wishes to announce that all disciplinary proceedings relating to freedom of expression, the expression of views, public criticism and peaceful assembly at all public universities shall be stopped with immediate effect,” it said.
The ministry said such freedoms must be exercised alongside responsibility and respect for the rule of law.
“Acts involving violence, vandalism, property damage, criminal offences, academic misconduct or breaches of legitimate disciplinary rules remain subject to the laws and regulations in force,” it said.
For the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) and Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), which are not governed by AUKU, the ministry said it would conduct a similar review of their respective provisions relating to students to align them with the reforms being implemented under AUKU.
MOHE said it remained committed to developing an open, structured and inclusive higher education governance system through the involvement of all stakeholders to ensure a quality higher education ecosystem for the country’s future.
* UUCA is the acronym for the Malay name of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU).

Title: Ahmad Zahid extends condolences to families of Nepal flood victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has expressed concern over the safety and well-being of Malaysians affected by the devastating floods in Nepal, hoping those still unaccounted for will be found safe and reunited with their families.
Ahmad Zahid also extended his condolences to families who lost loved ones in the disaster, while expressing solidarity with the people of Nepal.
“I am deeply saddened by the devastating flash floods in Nepal, which have claimed lives, displaced families and caused widespread destruction. My thoughts and prayers are with the people of Nepal, especially those who have lost loved ones and families still anxiously awaiting news of those who remain missing,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
He also prayed that ongoing search and rescue operations would be eased and those still in danger brought to safety.
“May every family affected by this tragedy be given strength and resilience in the days ahead,” he said.
According to a tally released by Nepal’s tourism board, as of 5.30 pm local time (7.45 pm Malaysian time) on Thursday, the death toll from the devastating floods rose to 359. — Bernama

Title: Putrajaya, six states across Malaysia at risk of worsening haze through Aug 31, MetMalaysia says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Several areas across Malaysia remain at risk of hazy conditions and reduced visibility from August 27 to 31, according to weather forecast models monitored by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
MetMalaysia director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the conditions were due to the influence of south-westerly winds and a persistently high number of hotspots in southern Sumatra and western Kalimantan.
“The MyCMAQ (Malaysia Community Multi-scale Air Quality Model) haze concentration forecast shows Sarawak could be the worst-affected area, with most districts expected to experience hazy weather at the Unhealthy level.
“Several districts could also reach the Very Unhealthy level on August 30 and 31,” he said in a statement today.
He said hazy conditions were expected in Sabah from Saturday, while high haze concentrations could affect Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya until August 31.

Title: Kuching storm blows off roof at Sarawak deputy premier’s family home
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 28 — The roof of Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Dr Sim Kui Hian’s family house was blown off in a storm that hit several areas in Kuching yesterday.
In a Facebook post, Dr Sim said he was in Bintulu when the incident occurred and was thankful that everyone at the house was safe.
He said several houses in the surrounding areas, including a mall, were also affected by the storm.
“Thank you very much to all the messages concerning the roof of my family house that was blown off by the storm,” according to the post.
He also thanked the Malaysia Civil Defence Force (APM), the Fire and Rescue Department, Sarawak Energy and other agencies for their prompt response and assistance following the incident. — Bernama

Title: Viral video of cockroaches in food container prompts DBKL to shut BBQ outlet for 14 days (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — A video showing several insects believed to be cockroaches crawling inside a food container at a barbecue restaurant in the capital went viral on social media yesterday.
The footage, shared by a Threads user through the @aqilahmaria_ account, showed several of the insects inside a container holding raw meat near a container of prawns,
Berita Harian
reported.
The user claimed the incident had left her traumatised and reminded the public to check their food before eating it.
“Incident yesterday (the day before). I’m traumatised! I was hungry and then saw something like this. Before eating, check your food first,” she wrote.
Following the video’s circulation and attention on social media, Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) conducted an inspection of the premises.
DBKL, in a reply to the user’s post, said its Premises Sanitation Unit under the Titiwangsa Zone 5 Health Office, Health and Environment Department, carried out a follow-up inspection following the complaint.
DBKL said the premises was ordered to close under the Food Establishment Licensing By-Laws (Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur) 2016, effective from August 26 to September 9, 2026.
“The closure is to allow the relevant party to carry out corrective measures and thorough cleaning.
“DBKL will always strive to ensure food premises in Kuala Lumpur comply with hygiene and public health requirements, while protecting the interests and safety of city residents,” it said.

Title: Two killed in Proton X70 crash while fleeing police checkpoint in Gua Musang
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Aug 28 — Two men were killed in a road crash after the SUV they were travelling in veered into the opposite lane, collided with another vehicle and then crashed into a lamp post on Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Lipis in Bukit Lanjut yesterday.
Gua Musang district police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said police received a report about the crash at 10.24 am.
He said initial investigations found that police officers were conducting snap checks at Kilometre 16 of Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Lipis when they spotted a suspicious-looking Proton X70, which then turned back towards Gua Musang town.
"Police officers then followed the vehicle to carry out an inspection. Upon reaching the scene, the Proton X70 is believed to have lost control, crossed into the opposite lane and collided with the rear side of a Toyota Hilux before veering off the road and crashing into a lamp post,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Sik said one man died at the scene, while another died while receiving treatment at Gua Musang Hospital. Their bodies were then taken to the hospital’s forensic unit for post-mortem examinations.
He said several other occupants of the Proton X70 were injured and taken to the same hospital for treatment, adding that the police officers and the Toyota Hilux driver were not injured.
"Further investigations are under way to identify all those involved and establish the full circumstances of the incident,” he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving. — Bernama

Title: Haze worsens as 18 areas across Malaysia, including KL, Putrajaya, record unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Air quality worsened across the country this morning, with 18 areas recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 7am.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Sri Aman in Sarawak recorded the highest API reading at 189, followed by Serian at 168.
Sarikei and Miri also recorded unhealthy readings of 152 and 102 respectively.
In the Klang Valley, Cheras and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded API readings of 159 and 153 respectively, while Putrajaya recorded a reading of 152.
Three areas in Selangor — Johan Setia (155), Shah Alam (153) and Petaling Jaya (147) — were also in the unhealthy category, along with Seremban in Negri Sembilan at 104.
Unhealthy readings were also recorded in Penang at Seberang Perai (156), Minden (154) and Seberang Jaya (152); in Perak at Taiping (154), Tasek Ipoh (133) and Seri Manjung (106); and in Kedah at Sungai Petani (152).
Two days ago, the Cabinet decided to review the scale and locations of this year’s National Day celebrations on August 31 following the haze affecting several areas, including Putrajaya, Kuala Lumpur and Sarawak.
Last night, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said hazy conditions are expected in Sabah from Saturday, while high haze concentrations could affect Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya until August 31.
MetMalaysia said this was based on weather forecast models, which showed the influence of south-westerly winds and a persistently high number of hotspots in southern Sumatra and western Kalimantan.

Title: Temenggor, Gerik hit by 3.4-magnitude earthquake
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — A weak 3.4-magnitude earthquake struck the Temenggor area in Gerik, Perak at 12.06am today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
MetMalaysia said the earthquake occurred at a depth of 10km at coordinates 5.5 degrees North and 101.3 degrees East, reported Astro Awani.
The epicentre was detected about 9km north-east of Hulu Perak, it said.
Tremors were reportedly felt in several areas around Gerik.
There were no immediate reports of damage or injuries from the incident.
MetMalaysia said it would continue monitoring the situation and provide updates should there be any further developments.
